transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in today?
Over the last month I’ve just lost interest in my art, dancing, and even my job. I can’t seem to care about anything the way I used to.
Have you been feeling down or losing interest like this most days for more than two years, or did it start only within the past month?

It hasn't been going on for two years, but it's been longer than just a month. This current heavy, low feeling—and the swings I've had before it—has actually been going on steadily for about five months now. It all really started around the time our intense tax season ramped up.
Did these symptoms start only after the tax-season stress, and have they improved at all when the stress eased? Or have they continued even when things were calmer?

During the tax rush, I actually had this huge burst of intense energy, but once that ended, I just crashed into this heavy low instead of going back to normal. Even though work is much calmer now, this flat, empty feeling has continued steadily for about five months without getting any better.

Before the tax season stress started, were you feeling mostly normal, or had the low mood and loss of interest already been present for at least two weeks? Also, since the stress eased, have your symptoms continued without much improvement?

Before the tax season, I was feeling completely normal, and this heavy low mood only hit me after the busy rush ended. Since then, even though work has calmed down, I haven't felt any improvement and have been stuck like this for about five months now.
Have you also had other symptoms like changes in sleep, appetite, energy, concentration, or feelings of guilt or worthlessness during this low period?

Yes, I've been tossing and turning all night worrying about work mistakes, and I have to force myself to eat to the point where my pants are getting loose. I also feel completely drained of energy, struggle to focus on simple emails, and feel incredibly guilty and useless for letting everyone down.

Did these symptoms begin only after the stressful tax season ended, or have they continued even when you were not under that stress? Also, have they been present most days for at least two weeks without a clear break?

This low feeling started right after the busy tax rush ended, and it has continued even though the work stress has cleared up. It has been there every single day without any break for about five months now.
Have you had any thoughts that life is not worth living, or thoughts of hurting yourself or ending your life?
No, I haven't had any thoughts of hurting myself or ending my life. Even though I feel really empty and down, I've never felt like life isn't worth living.

During the time when you had that huge burst of energy, did you also need much less sleep, feel unusually confident or irritable, talk more than usual, or do risky things that were out of character for you?

Yes, during that phase I only slept three or four hours a night but felt wide awake, and I got really snappy if anyone tried to slow me down. I felt incredibly confident, like I was the only one who truly understood our clients' finances, and talked so fast my coworkers joked I'd had too much coffee. I didn't do anything risky or dangerous, but I was definitely operating at an unusually intense, fast pace.

Have you ever had a period of at least 4 days when you felt unusually energized or irritable like that, with less need for sleep, more talkative than usual, racing thoughts, or increased activity, even if it did not cause major problems?

Yes, I definitely had a period like that that lasted for about two weeks during the tax season. I was highly energized on just three to four hours of sleep, my thoughts were racing with new business ideas, and I was talking a mile a minute while taking on way too many tasks at once.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient has a clear history of a distinct hypomanic episode lasting about 2 weeks (decreased need for sleep, increased energy, pressured/rapid speech, racing thoughts, increased goal-directed activity, irritability, grandiosity) followed by a persistent depressive episode lasting about 5 months with anhedonia, low mood/emptiness, insomnia, decreased appetite/weight loss, low energy, poor concentration, and excessive guilt. This pattern is most consistent with bipolar affective disorder, currently depressed, with a prior hypomanic episode. Unipolar major depressive disorder is less likely because of the hypomanic history, and an adjustment disorder is less likely because symptoms persisted well beyond the stressor and met syndromal mood-episode criteria.
